episodes.164477: The Ozarks were on the western edge of a severe thunderstorm and tornado outbreak that occurred from the evening of the 10th to the early morning of the 11th. A very unstable and highly sheared airmass interacted with a strong cold front and upper level disturbance to spark the widespread storm activity. According to the NWS Storm Prediction Center, 121 tornadoes occurred from southwest Missouri eastward into northeast Arkansas, Kentucky, Tennessee, and Illinois.  Three tornadoes, each rated EF-1, occurred near West Branson, Walnut Shade and Niangua. In addition, there were over 30 reports of damaging wind gusts over 60 mph, and several reports with hail up to golf ball size. Due to the fast movement of the storms, rainfall accumulations were generally one half inch or less.
episodes.164587: A warm front lift northward across central Alabama and produced just enough instability and shear for the development of a weak tornado in Elmore County.
episodes.164616: A slow moving warm front combined with several upper level disturbances generated clusters of showers and thunderstorms that produced locally heavy rain and flooding.
episodes.165267: A severe storm in Collin County produced quarter-sized hail.

events.narrative: River Road was washed out near Brady Road due to a rapid rise of the nearby Styx River. The nearby Styx River gauge at Smith's Landing rose 10 feet from 11pm on the 9th to 9am on the 10th.

National Weather Service meteorologists surveyed damage in Elmore County and determined that it was consistent with an EF0 tornado, with maximum winds near 70 mph.  A brief tornado occurred on the northern side of Albritton Lane just northeast of Montgomery and southeast of Wetumpka. One home had a section of roofing and soffit blown off, and another home had numerous shingles removed. Two separate sections of fencing were knocked over as well. Another home had some roofing blown off a back porch.

Microburst winds estimated between 60 and 70 mph produced localized damage. A modular home had siding removed and a small barn had a portion of its roof removed. Several trees had tops broken off and large limbs down. A MODoT electric sign was also knocked over.
Minor roof damage occurred to a barn.
A home suffered minor roof damage and a utility shed was moved off its foundation.
Two utility poles were reported snapped.
Winds estimated at 60 mph were reported.
Winds estimated at 70 mph were reported.
